title: A Local AI Lane for Contoso

slides.title: A Local AI Lane for Contoso
slides.subtitle: Local drafting alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot
slides.takeaway: Test a local drafting lane while keeping Microsoft 365 Copilot in place.
slides.notes: Approve a 10-user, 2-week pilot of Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark for traveling consultants. The opportunity is sensitive, repeated drafting from interview notes and site documents. Microsoft 365 Copilot stays in place. We will measure task time, draft quality and user experience before making a broader decision.

slides.title: The Road Creates Drafting Friction
slides.takeaway: Repeated summaries and restricted Wi-Fi make local drafting worth testing.
slides.notes: Contoso has 4,000 employees, including 1,200 traveling consultants. Each writes about 6 client summaries weekly, taking about 25 minutes to draft each. About 30% of client sites restrict guest Wi-Fi. Sensitive interview notes and site documents make the processing location important, alongside the time spent drafting.

slides.title: An Office That Travels With You
slides.takeaway: Bring drafting to the documents; validate disconnected use during the pilot.
slides.notes: Think of a portable office: the assistant and selected working papers travel together on the laptop. Stage the required model and approved files before leaving. The intended local drafting path keeps processing on-device. The pilot validates disconnected use and checks the actual data path before broader adoption.

slides.title: Add a Lane, Keep Copilot
slides.takeaway: Microsoft 365 Copilot stays; local AI adds a complementary drafting lane.
slides.notes: This is an addition, not a migration. Keep Microsoft 365 Copilot and existing subscriptions. Use the local lane for sensitive, repeated drafting from selected local materials. Cloud-connected work remains in established workflows. The pilot tests whether the added lane is useful, without assuming financial or licensing benefits.

slides.title: A Local Path for Sensitive Drafts
slides.takeaway: Selected files, prompts and drafts stay on-device within the proposed local lane.
slides.notes: The proposed local boundary contains selected files, prompts, the drafting app, its open model and draft review. NVIDIA RTX Spark supplies local compute. Microsoft 365 Copilot remains a separate companion lane; the diagram does not imply automatic document transfer. Validate the configuration, data handling and disconnected use during the pilot.

slides.title: The Device Behind the Local Lane
slides.takeaway: Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark hosts the local drafting stack.
slides.notes: The supplied device is Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark, a Blackwell RTX GPU, 20 CPU cores and 128 GB installed memory. Its local catalog contains 28 open models. Hardware establishes the test platform; it does not prove draft quality, battery life or time savings.

slides.title: Device Speed Is Not Task Success
slides.takeaway: Decode benchmarks are signals; the pilot must establish drafting quality and task time.
slides.notes: These figures measure text-generation throughput, not completed summaries. Local-AI-Bench, October 2026, reports about 72 tokens per second for Gemma 4 26B and 86 for Qwen3-Coder 30B, single stream on this device. They do not establish draft quality or model suitability; the pilot tests practical outcomes.

slides.title: A First Draft Needs an Editor
slides.takeaway: Use local AI for a starting draft; the consultant remains accountable.
slides.notes: Treat the assistant like a junior writer with a source packet, not a source of truth. It can propose a draft, but the consultant checks source fidelity, omissions, confidentiality and tone before sharing. Draft-quality review is part of the pilot; fast output alone is not success.

slides.title: Capacity Worth Measuring, Not Promising
slides.takeaway: 27,600 hours annually is an illustrative estimate to validate, not a commitment.
slides.notes: The brief's illustrative annualization uses 1,200 consultants, 6 summaries weekly, a hypothetical 5 minutes saved per summary and 46 working weeks to estimate 27,600 hours annually. This is unvalidated capacity, not a financial claim or commitment. Measure the real task-time difference and preserve draft quality before considering any extrapolation.

slides.title: Test the Complete Drafting Task
slides.takeaway: Measure the whole task, including review, under connected and disconnected conditions.

steps.label: Draft
steps.detail: Exercise connected and disconnected local drafting

steps.label: Review
steps.detail: Check source fidelity and client-ready tone

steps.label: Measure
steps.detail: Record task time, quality and user experience

slides.notes: Use representative interview notes and site documents that Contoso authorizes. Compare the current workflow with local-assisted drafting on matched tasks. Include review time, judge source fidelity and capture user feedback. Validate disconnected use and local data handling. Keep Microsoft 365 Copilot available for its existing role throughout the pilot.

slides.title: Make the Pilot Decision-Ready
slides.takeaway: Proposed plan: 10 users, 2 weeks, then an evidence-based sponsor decision.
slides.notes: Proposed ownership: the CIO validates the local configuration and data handling; the Consulting lead selects representative work and assesses quality; the COO reviews task-time and experience findings. After 2 weeks, sponsors decide whether to expand, adjust or stop. No rollout or benefit is assumed before evidence is reviewed.

slides.title: Approve a Measured Start
slides.takeaway: Authorize the pilot, not a rollout or a promised capacity gain.

steps.label: Agree the scorecard
steps.detail: Task time, draft quality and user experience

slides.notes: Approve a 10-user, 2-week pilot of Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark for local drafting alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot. Confirm authorized client materials and the scorecard before launch. Bring task-time, draft-quality, user-experience and disconnected-use evidence back to the sponsors for the next decision.
